newsitem.title: CHINA: World Bank sets loans for China education.
newsitem.headline: World Bank sets loans for China education.

text.p: The World Bank said on Thursday it would extend $85 million in low-interest loans to China to finance education for girls and members of ethnic minority groups to help lift them out of poverty.
The project would help some 6.2 million children in more than 90 poor counties.

Local governments would contribute another $80.2 million to the project, which would build or renovate primary and secondary schools, provide books and improve the quality of teachers, the bank said in a statement made available to Reuters.
The loans, due to mature in 35 years, carry annual interest of 1.2 percent or less.

The funds would be spent in the southern island province of Hainan, Shanxi in the north, Heilongjiang in the northeast, Yunnan in the southwest and the southern provinces of Guizhou and Hunan, the bank said.
Education in those areas was marked by poorly equipped classrooms, inadequately trained teachers, lack of teaching materials and higher drop-out rates, the bank said.
The project would benefit 44,000 schools and 138,000 teachers in areas where the levels of education and economic development were lower than the national average.
While China has made rapid strides in expanding its economy, many women and members of ethnic minorities have been left behind.
Up to 70 percent of China's 160 million illiterate and semi-literate people are women.
China's urban poor totalled 11.76 million at the end of 1996, according to official figures.
China has set a poverty line for urban residents at 1,700 yuan ($204) per capita per year and needs 4.2 billion yuan this year in poverty alleviation funds.
